newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Times Of India
CONSENSUS LIKELY IN CONGRESS LEADERSHIP TUSSLE

Possibility of a consensus in choosing the new Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader has brightened. Chances of an election by secret ballot to decide the CPP leadership issue receded, following the announcement of a CPP general body meeting, not a poll notification, on January 3. The move followed groundswell of support for party president Sitaram Kesri. Important party functionaries, Members of Parliament and state party units pledged their support for Kesri. Ironically, the announcement for the CPP meeting came in response to Congress Working Committee member Rajesh Pilot's call for formal notification of the poll schedule.
The Economic Times
TELECOM MAJOR PLANS GDR EARLY NEXT YEAR

Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's (VSNL) much delayed and once aborted $1 billion Global Depository Receipt (GDR) issue is likely to be launched in late January or early February 1997. The telecommunication major has set a deadline of January 7 for roping in four syndicate members in addition to the lead management syndicate of Jardine Fleming, Kleinwort Benson and Salomon Brothers. The move has come in the wake of a Union Cabinet decision saying that the syndicate of lead managers for VSNL's GDR issue ought to be expanded.
INSURANCE WATCHDOG TO OVERHAUL SECTOR

The Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) is planning to overhaul accounting norms for the insurance sector and in the surplus distribution procedures of Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The IRA move is seen as a first step towards restructuring the public sector insurance industry. The IRA is also looking at the possibility of revamping the method of sharing the surplus of LIC in a manner that it helps the latter boost its equity capital through the creation of reserves.
PREFERENTIAL SHARE ALLOTMENT POLICY DRAWS FLAK

The Delhi High Court issued show-cause notices to the government and the apex bank (RBI) on a public interest litigation. The litigation challenges the RBI policy of allowing allotment of preferential share to 212 foreign companies to enable them to raise their equity share in Indian companies to 51 percent. The petitioner, a practising lawyer, said the lacunae lay in the provision of allowing companies to allot preferential shares to foreign partners on the basis of special resolutions passed by shareholders. BANK OF BARODA CUTS DEPOSIT RATES

Bank of Baroda cut its term deposit rates by between two to one percentage point following the cut in its prime lending rate. Rates on deposits for between 30 to 45 days have been cut by two percentage points from eight to six percent. Rates on deposits between 46 to 179 days have been reduced from nine to eight percent and 180 days up to one year from 10 to nine percent. Long-term deposits of over three years continue to attract 12.5 percent. The rate on Non-Resident Non-Repatriable (NRNR) deposits of up to one year was reduced to 15.5 percent and for deposits of one to three years to 15 percent.
RAIDS NOT ON AGENDA OF PM'S MEET WITH BUSINESS CLUBS

A 15-point agenda has been prepared by the prime minister's office for his December 31 meeting with the three apex industry clubs. These include the role of state governments, tax structure, tariff policy, liquidity position, foreign direct investment, interest rates, growth of exports and resource mobilisation, among others. However, the issue of raids on corporate houses, a sore point among all the chambers, does not figure on the official agenda. All the apex chambers have been critical of the policies and actions of the United Front government. Therefore, a free and frank exchange of thoughts is expected at the meeting.
CABINET ACCEPTS SEVEN PCT GROWTH RATE FOR NINTH PLAN

The Cabinet accepted the seven percent growth rate for the Ninth Plan period, Planning Commission deputy chairman Madhu Dandavate said. To achieve this the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) would extend substantial benefits to small sectors. The concessions would also be extended to certain capital and labour intensive industries to optimise employment generation during the Ninth Plan. The government's Employment Assurance Scheme would also be universally adopted, said Dandavate.
Financial Express
APEX BANK CUTS CASH RESERVE RATIO BY ONE PCT

Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, announced a two-stage, one percentage point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR). The CRR cut would be effective from fortnights beginning on January 4 and January 18. RBI sources said the cut would inject 42.75 billion rupees into the system. The cut followed RBI governor C. Rangarajan's announcement in the October-March credit policy statement that the CRR cut would be contingent on the monetary and price situation in the country. The liquidity induced after the cut would bring down the interbank overnight rates, currently hovering between 10.9 and 11.25 percent, bank dealers said.
LAW MINISTRY STAND MAY NIP STOCK LENDING SCHEME

The stock lending scheme, formulated by the stock market regulator (SEBI) and backed by the finance ministry, seems to have come a cropper. Finance ministry and SEBI officials have come to the conclusion that the scheme may not be viable because of the Law Ministry stipulation that the shares, which have been lent out, will have to be returned in order to ensure that the lender does not attract the provisions of the capital gains tax. The scheme is now expected to be referred back to the Union Law Ministry for a second opinion.
TOYOTA IN TALKS WITH KIRLOSKAR

Japanese automobile major Toyota is negotiating with Kirloskar to set up a joint venture for manufacturing cars in India. A feasibility study is currently under way by Toyota and Kirloskar. Though details have yet to be worked out, Toyota hopes to conclude the study by the end of this year and analyse the results. Sources said the joint venture, to be established next summer, would manufacture recreational vehicles and passenger cars at an annual rate of 100,000 vehicles, starting as early as 1999.
Business Standard
POWER FINANCE CORP TO DIVERSIFY INTO BANKING

Power Finance Corporation (PFC) is planning to diversify into fuel, transport, banking, merchant banking, mutual funds and insurance sectors. By diversifying into these sectors, PFC plans to tap projects with short gestation periods which offer better returns. The diversification is linked to a $465 million loan from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank to PFC. The nodal power financing agency has also decided to finance projects which are indirectly linked to power projects. Through such moves, it hopes to have a judicious balance of short and long-term projects in its basket, thereby decreasing the risk related to financing power projects.
BANKS TOLD TO HOLD PROMOTERS' SHARES TILL LOANS ARE REPAID

Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, directed the banks and financial institutions to take custody of the shares of the promoters, who had taken term loans to prevent them from diluting their commitment to projects. The decision was taken pursuant to the recommendations of the estimates committee of the Lok Sabha. Bankers said the reason for the RBI directive was to prevent promoters from offloading their stake in the companies they owned.
TELECOM MAJOR PUTS OFF DECISION ON JOINT VENTURE

The Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) board of directors put off decision on VSNL's $500-million joint venture proposal with British Telecom to develop India as a regional hub for Internet traffic. Sources said although the board would discuss the proposal early next month, the joint venture was unlikely to be cleared before the scheduled visit of British Prime Minister John Major on January 9. The proposal envisaged all call, data, video and Internet traffic from the Middle East, South Asia and South-East Asia being routed through India. Similarly, traffic bound for this region would come into India and be distributed to these countries.
Business Line
KINETIC GROUP, KOREAN FIRM TIE UP FOR CABLES

The 10-billion rupee Kinetic group tied-up with Samyeong Cables of South Korea for manufacturing control cables. A substantial portion of the production would be used in-house for the two wheelers produced by the Kinetic group, company sources said. Samyeong, an original equipment supplier to Hyundai in Korea, was scouting for a local partner after Hyundai's entry into the Indian market. Kinetic already has a tie-up with Hyundai under a joint venture company for manufacturing vertical transportation systems and escalators.
ARBITRATION RULES TO BE REVISED

The Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA), under the commerce ministry, will revise its Rules of Arbitration to bring them in line with the new arbitration and conciliation law. The commerce, industry and law ministries have also responded positively to the use of ICA arbitration clause in resolving commercial disputes. One of the key features of the new law relates to the appointment of arbitrators by the Chief Justices of High Courts. In case the parties in dispute are unable to agree on the procedure for such appointments, the Chief Justice is also empowered to designate any person or institution to take necessary steps for the appointment of arbitrators.
